pages.title: Diminishing Returns
pages.text: Eating the same food repeatedly gives less and less nutrition each time. This is called $(thing)diminishing returns$().$(br2)The more often you eat a specific food, the lower its nutritional value becomes. Returns recover naturally over time — the longer you go without eating something, the more nutrition it gives when you eat it again.

pages.title: Novelty Bonus
pages.text: Eating a food you haven't had in a long time — or ever — gives a $(thing)novelty bonus$(). This bonus decays as you eat the same food more frequently.$(br2)The takeaway: variety is always rewarded. Rotate your foods and you will consistently get better nutrition than eating the same thing every meal.
